title: Runtime Execution Cascades and Soft-Fail Synthesis
author: Amina Patel
content:
Summary:

This handbook defines the "execution cascade" model we adopted in 2027 for orchestrating multi-tier inference execution, how kernels and scheduler policies participate in graceful degradation, and the operational playbooks for profiling and benchmarking cascade behaviors. It is intended for runtime engineers, SREs, and product owners responsible for model rollouts, SLA preservation, and incident mitigation.

Why an execution cascade?

- Modern inference requires cross-layer coordination: model variants, kernel capabilities, KV cache state, and router-level routing all affect end-to-end latency and quality.
- The execution cascade formalizes ordered fallback steps (fastest/cheapest -> compatible fallbacks -> degraded modes) and the safety checks and instrumentation needed to avoid quality regression or outage.

Scope and assumptions:

- Applies to Redwood hosted + Dedicated runtime pools.
- Assumes models are registered with a variant graph (primary, low-latency quantized, high-fidelity CPU fallback).
- Assumes runtime kernel telemetry (kernel_id, slot_id, preempt_count) and request traces are emitted to the observability pipeline.

1) Conceptual model

Execution cascade layers (top-down):

1. Serve fast: low-latency GPU kernels (best throughput, quantized).
2. Serve fallback-1: compatible kernel variant (slower but high fidelity).
3. Serve fallback-2: CPU or remote microservice for short-tail completions.
4. Degraded response: length-limited generation + structured error with explicit quality flag.

Key properties:

- Deterministic ordering: cascades are declared per-model and pinned at route level.
- Circuit breakers and hysteresis: transition thresholds use smoothing windows to avoid oscillation.
- Quality gates: each downgrade step must pass an automated eval suite before being allowed in the graph.

2) Runtime integration: scheduler and kernel interaction

Scheduling primitives used in cascades:

- Slot reservation: short-term exclusive kernel slots are reserved for high-priority fast-path requests.
- Soft-preempt windows: kernels expose a preemptability flag; scheduler will only preempt if preempt_count < N and no active KV update operations exist.
- Credit buckets: each tenant has a credit balance for fast-path tokens; negative balance triggers cascade routing.

Example scheduler policy (YAML):

policy_name: cascade-alpha
fast_path:
  kernel_selector: "gpu-quantized-v2"
  token_credit_threshold: 1000
  preempt_policy: "soft"
fallbacks:
  - kernel_selector: "gpu-fp16-v1"
    max_seq_len: 512
  - kernel_selector: "cpu-approximate"
    max_seq_len: 256
rollout:
  canary_ratio: 0.02
  smoothing_window_ms: 30000

(Copy/paste safe YAML shown above).

3) Profiling playbook for cascade behavior

Objective: capture pre- and post-degradation traces that highlight where requests moved through the cascade and why.

Telemetry to collect:

- Request timeline (router_enqueue, kernel_dispatch, kernel_complete, response_emit) in ms.
- Kernel attributes: kernel_id, binary_version, occupancy_pct, sm_util, preempt_count.
- KV cache metrics: hit_rate, warmup_time_ms, eviction_count.
- Route decisions: route_reason (credit_exhausted, kernel_unavailable, model_quality_fallback).

Sampling strategy:

- Stratified sampling by latency bucket: p50/p95/p99 and by route variant.
- Correlate any tail events with kernel switch events.

Investigation steps:

1. Reproduce with a synthetic corpus mirroring production tokens-per-request and sequence length distribution. Use the workload-replay tool:

redwoodctl replay --target cascade-alpha --corpus s3://replay-buckets/corpus-2028-01 --concurrency 200 --duration 10m

2. Enable verbose kernel traces for a 5 minute window: set kernel_trace_rate=1.
3. Export traces to traceviz and build a waterfall view focused on requests that encountered >1 fallback.

Root causes commonly found:

- Credit exhaustion due to aggressive burst traffic from a single route.
- Kernel binary mismatch causing deterministic rejection; scheduler then routes to fallback.
- Subtle latency amplification from slot-slicing under mixed small/large sequence workloads.

4) Benchmark protocol for validating cascade safety

Goal: measure impact of cascading on p99 latency, token cost, and quality relative to baseline.

Bench steps (standardized):

- Baseline: run model on fast-path solo for 30m, measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
- Integrated: enable cascade graph and run same corpus for 30m.
- Stress: inject a synthetic burst (10x baseline RPS) for 2 minutes, observe transition time and hysteresis.

Metrics to record (CSV):

- timestamp, route, variant, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_sec, kernel_occupancy_pct, kvcache_hit_rate, quality_score_delta

Pass criteria for rollout gate:

- p99 increase < 1.5x baseline AND
- average quality_score_delta <= 0.03 (on the canonical eval set) AND
- cascade transition time <= 45s for burst stress test

5) Release and canary checklist (runtime + scheduling ops)

Pre-release:

- Verify model variant graph is registered and has quality metadata.
- Confirm kernel binary compatibility matrix for all targeted accelerators.
- Register scheduler policy in the staging cluster and run the benchmark protocol.

Canary rollout steps:

1. Deploy policy to 1% of traffic in staging for 1h. Validate metrics.
2. Expand to 2% in production for 30m; run quick health checks and smoke tests.
3. Observe circuit breakers: if any of the following triggers, rollback automatically:
   - sustained p99 > 2x baseline for 10m
   - KV cache warmup failure (hit_rate < 20% after 10m)
   - quality gate breached (automated eval threshold)

Commands (examples):

# attach policy to route
redwoodctl routing apply --route my-service-chat --policy cascade-alpha

# monitor canary metrics
redwoodctl metrics tail --route my-service-chat --window 15m --filters p99,kvcache_hit_rate,quality_delta

6) Operational runbooks (quick actions)

A. Detecting unintended cascade amplification

1. Symptom: p99 spikes while fast-path occupancy down; multiple requests show fallback_reason=credit_exhausted.
2. Action: increase token_credit_threshold by 50% for the route, or temporarily reassign to higher-capacity pool.
3. Long-term: adjust per-tenant burst throttle and improve prewarming of KV cache for the heavy route.

B. Kernel binary incompatibility (hard rejections)

1. Symptom: kernel_dispatch fails with error code KERN_BIN_MISMATCH; router jumps to fallback-1.
2. Action: pin router to older kernel binary until new binary rollout completes.
2a. redwoodctl kernel rollback --binary gpu-quantized-v2 --to gpu-quantized-v1

C. Degraded response observed (quality flag set)

1. Symptom: increased 'quality_flag: degraded' in responses and customer complaints.
2. Action: route traffic to primary variant for VIP customers and open a regression investigation ticket.

7) Known issues observed (non-exhaustive)

- Soft-fail amplification under opcode mismatch (INC-2027-1420): certain kernel ops return transient opcode-mapping errors which cause repeated fallback loops for small batches. Mitigation: apply opcode compatibility shim (deployable via kernel plugin) and add a short-lived blacklist for the offending kernel instance.
- Quant-crossover drift: repeated model re-quantizations during long canaries cause small quality drift detectable by the eval harness. Mitigation: enforce quantization-stability check in the model onboarding pipeline.
- Slot-slicing tail spikes: when mixing tiny chat completions with long-document summaries, slot-slicing can starve large requests and increase their p99. Mitigation: enforce separate slot pools per workload shape or enable sequence-length-aware admission.

8) Post-incident diagnostics checklist

- Export request traces for the 30 minutes before and after the detected spike.
- Correlate with kernel rollout events and scheduler policy changes.
- Run the parallel replay at 2x concurrency to validate the hypothesised mitigation.
- Update the cascade policy (token thresholds, hysteresis) and re-run the benchmark protocol.

9) Ownership and escalation

- Primary owners: runtime-scheduler team (oncall: runtime-scheduler@redwood.internal)
- Secondary: serving-runtime-infra team (oncall: serving-infra@redwood.internal)
- Escalation: if customer-impacting (> 5% failed requests or p99 > 2x baseline for > 30m) alert Platform Incident Manager and set incident severity to Sev2.

10) Appendix: templates and helpers

A) Incident tag sample (use in issue tracker):

labels: [runtime-cascade, kernel-fallback, priority-high]
summary: "cascade amplification — route=my-service-chat — observed 4x p99"

B) Quick YAML for sequence-aware admission (example):

admission:
  policy: sequence-aware
  buckets:
    - max_seq: 128
      pool: small-slot-pool
    - max_seq: 1024
      pool: large-slot-pool

C) Benchmark CSV header (copy into bench-scripts):

timestamp,route,variant,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,tokens_per_sec,kernel_occupancy_pct,kvcache_hit_rate,quality_score_delta
